items.title: Glucose hypometabolism gates tau-dependent necroptosis
items.author: Maria Livia Sassano, Bart De Strooper
items.content: <article>Tau pathology closely tracks neuronal loss in Alzheimer’s disease, but how phosphorylated tau becomes lethal has remained unclear. Chen et al. identify a dual-hit mechanism: glucose hypometabolism removes a protective A20-mediated brake on necroptosis while phosphorylated tau scaffolds RIPK1 activation, driving tau-associated neuronal death.</article>

items.title: Decoding the sleeping mind with AI
items.author: Flavio Jean Schmidig, Yuval Nir
items.content: <article>The sleeping brain processes memory-related semantic information, yet decoding such content remains challenging. Combining a large, openly shared sleep EEG dataset with neural contrastive learning, Chen et al., in this issue of Neuron, establish a promising framework for non-invasive decoding of the sleeping human mind.</article>
